page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 7.75 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier single-core Geekbench scores, particularly in text processing, and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the weaker tier. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with large-block read and write operations registering in the bottom 25% of tested configurations. Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations similarly reflect lower-tier performance profiles.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the c4-highmem-4 is structured for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity relative to compute power, such as caching layers, lightweight database tasks, and text processing pipelines. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions provides hardware acceleration for small-scale machine learning inference, as demonstrated by average-tier performance in 135M and 7B parameter LLM prompt processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense memory allocation on a modern architecture, though its lower multi-threaded and memory bandwidth performance suggests it is less configured for highly parallelized, memory-bound compute tasks.
